title: RAW: complete f76v continuation and first-entry distinction under all71 frozen music values, with two fixed negation scopes
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_TESTED. Complete exploratory55-group descendant of the separately registered RAW490 selection:18 frozen types at32 positions plus exactly20 new values at23 positions;11 new clause productions and10 explicit binding conventions. It prescribes whole-part repetition and lower-pes phase continuity through later entries, then distinguishes first-entry times. FIRST_ENTRY_EVENT(r) and FIRST_ENTRY_TIME(qokaiin) have fixed typed denotations across their repeated uses. Positive and prohibitive final-scope variants are both retained before testing. No existing word, source branch, performer, part, exception or old paragraph is changed.

frozen_operators.SING: Execute successive note/rest events of the performer's own assigned part on that performer's local clock. Same operator for C06 leader and C09 lower pes; the argument-owned part changes the trace.
frozen_operators.REPEAT: After the complete current part, restart that part from its beginning on the same voice clock, with no added delay or new singer. Same operator for following rota singers in C02 and the two pes in C03.
frozen_operators.TOGETHER: Assert onset equality for the subject set; preserve all individual part identities and local clock trajectories.
frozen_operators.ENTER: Single inactive-to-active transition of a rota singer at its first prescribed onset. A later part repeat is not a second ENTER.
frozen_operators.WHEN: Create an event dependency using a resolved owner and cue, not a free equal-time spacing or textual adjacency relation.
frozen_operators.PAUSE: A rest is a duration-carrying event with its written owner/location. Internal versus terminal is topological, not equal-half duration.
frozen_operators.NO_END_PAUSE: Forbid an added terminal rest on P2; do not delete P2's already written internal rest.

frozen_newer_operators.INITIAL_ONSET: A TIME reference T0 belonging to the explicitly shared performance.
frozen_newer_operators.CO_ONSET(A,B): Require every first-start event in nonempty typed sets A and B to have equal time; no identity fusion or later phase reset.
frozen_newer_operators.BEGIN_BOTH_PES(pair): Return the two first StartPart event terms for the fixed pair [U,L], preserving their P1/P2 assignments.
frozen_newer_operators.START_NEXT_PES(pair,i): For 0<=i<2 return (StartPart(pair[i]),i+1); at i=2 a further call is undefined. The written two calls are not hardcoded to two unrelated names.
frozen_newer_operators.PRESERVE_OWN_CYCLE(v): Use assigned(v)'s complete ordered note/rest sequence and retained branch durations. The onset established for v determines later cycle boundaries. Other singers' ENTER events do not modify that cycle or clock.
frozen_newer_operators.IMMEDIATE_CYCLE_RESTART(v): At completion of assigned(v), restart it on v's existing clock without an added terminal rest, under the parent's unchanged need condition.
frozen_newer_operators.DISTINCT_GROUPS(A,B): Require A intersect B to be empty; preserve both already bound performer groups.
frozen_newer_operators.RESTATE: Reassert constraints on the same previously identified event term. It does not run an event again.
frozen_newer_operators.IDENTICAL_ROLE(a,b): Assert identity of same-sort HUMAN_PERFORMER referents, not similarity of names or parts.
frozen_newer_operators.WITHOUT_TERMINAL_REST(part): Require that the last event in the complete assigned written cycle is not REST. Do not delete, move or relabel any source event. P2 satisfies the source condition; an assigned cycle ending in REST does not.

ten_new_binding_conventions.rule: Explicit crossleaf content assumption: this new block concerns the same current performance specification as RAW487, sharing N,R0..R(N-1),U,L,M,P1,P2,X,T0 and unique event bank. No token here establishes that manuscript link; it is an openly unconfirmed extra identity assumption. This is not another source, new performer set, part reassignment or timing reset.

There are two fixed role ranges: F=R1..R(N-1), introduced by FOR_EACH FOLLOWER in F01, and Later=R2..R(N-1), denoted by old NEXT_FOLLOWER as in original C08. F07 reuses the named F extent; F05,F10,F11 use Later. All are explicit universal constructions. For N=2 Later is empty and these clauses have no instances; this is quantifier scope, not an unwritten leader exception.

The three r occurrences are one function e(x)=FIRST_ENTRY_EVENT(x): F05 first takes the currently quantified x, F05 second takes the explicitly written al(x), and F11 takes the explicitly final LEADER. No mutable role cursor or occurrence-specific value. qokaiin is one function time(e(x)); F06 takes LEADER and F10 applies that same function pointwise to its explicit (LEADER,x) pair.

F03's two-token nominal construction asserts U belongs to the already bound two-member PES group [U,L], with distinct human members. F04's four-token construction gives U a FIRST_PART_START time equal to the written ENTER(LEADER) at written T0. These are new surface constructions with implicit group/membership and first-part-start functions, counted as costs. They do not change the denotation of U, TWO, ENTER or T0, or manufacture another event.

F01 is a universally quantified rule for each full cycle of each follower's unchanged part M: completion, then zero-delay REPEAT. F05 CONTINUE uses the complete assigned part of written OTHER_MEMBER=L and the current later follower's e(x) as trigger. It preserves the existing part clock through that entry, including notes and rests; it does not assert that L is sounding a note at every instant. A natural part boundary can coincide with another singer's entry: the part's own restart remains permitted. What must stay unchanged is its source-derived cycle clock/origin and event sequence, not a raw phase number across its ordinary wrap.

Whole-block declaration mode is inherited: role/cue bindings are resolved before executing a schedule. F01 binds each follower's cue kind X; F07 binds that same cue to its predecessor owner. F06 RECALL and every event reference constrain existing unique first-event terms rather than executing another entry/start. No sentence order silently performs an extra action.

All three OTHERS_SILENT occurrences use the same Pending(R,t) definition. F02 adds a general invariant over states of the performance; F08 restricts its initially pending members to their individual waiting intervals [T0,time(e(f))); F09 evaluates the pending set after the entry batch triggered by the leader's first X attainment. Thus newly active R1 is not required to remain silent; all still-pending roles are. The new temporal scopes are declared, not lexical changes.

F09's WHEN takes explicitly written LEADER as owner and the already explicitly named X as cue. F11's WHEN SING construction quotes the unchanged SING operation as a description of the already prescribed leader-owned M process and queries its first X attainment. The final written LEADER supplies that owner. The query does not execute SING a second time or turn SING into a generic state label. This quotation and look-ahead owner binding are new grammar costs.

F10 binds a pair (R0,x) for each x in Later, applies FIRST_ENTRY_TIME pointwise and prohibits an existential common TIME tau satisfying the explicit AT_TIME and TOGETHER relation. ANY TIME is scoped inside the written NOT. F11 retains exactly that actor quantifier independent of the polarity boundary: first ENTER is e(x); second is explicitly IDENTIFIED_BY r(LEADER)=e0. The old leader exception is never copied into these new prohibitions.

Exactly11 clause spans and the listed reductions are hypothesized, not observed punctuation. F11 polarity has exactly the two predeclared alternatives below. In F11 CO_ONSET and TOGETHER both state equality of the same first-event onsets; both tokens are retained as semantically redundant assertions, not dropped as filler or counted as independent evidence. No unmarked event identity, new exception or modified production may be selected after testing. Extended negative scope is a declared distributive prohibition construction over the individual following relation assertions, not negation of a single conjunction. TOGETHER always receives the human subject set; the constructions explicitly associate those performers with the written first-event references. CO_ONSET retains event-set arguments.

fixed_scope_variants.F11: The later WHEN clause has positive polarity: on the same cue, assert CO_ONSET(e(x),e0) and TOGETHER for the exact same actor/event bindings. No role, word, event or source branch changes.

operator_application_contract.event_identity: e(v)=the one old ENTER(v) key for a rota performer. The new qokaiin function returns the existing event's time: qokaiin(v)=time(e(v)); no second freely adjustable time. FIRST_PART_START(U/L) are distinct typed keys supplied by unchanged parent/source.
operator_application_contract.repeat_and_continue: For each actual complete cycle instance of assigned(f), AFTER_COMPLETION and IMMEDIATELY constrain the existing REPEAT boundary. CONTINUE(assigned(L),e(x)) preserves L's phase before/after an entry; a written rest remains part of the cycle. No new source cycle length is fit. Keep the unchanged common performance-need and observation-window conventions. At a simultaneous natural end of P2, its own ordinary cycle restart is allowed; CONTINUE forbids only an entry-induced extra restart or changed clock origin. It does not equate two raw phase numbers across a legitimate modulo-cycle wrap.
operator_application_contract.time_quantification: F10 asserts not exists tau such that time(e0)=tau=time(e(x)), with the two references supplied by the written role pair and qokaiin. aiin takes the human performer subject set {R0,x} and states their common onset in this explicit first-entry context. It does not acquire a new generic event-set domain. char supplies the time sort; qo binds tau; cheedy attaches the explicit time references.
operator_application_contract.F11_identity_and_guard: Let g=first_reach(X,SING_process(R0,M)). Let a=e(x), b an ENTER term. Written qol identifies b with written r(LEADER)=e0. The conditional body is CO_ONSET({a},{b}) AND TOGETHER of human subjects {x,R0} in the explicit first-entry context. The first operator keeps event-set arguments; the second keeps performer subjects. Both yield the same onset-equality constraint here. Neither mentions later cycle restarts.
operator_application_contract.scope_of_no_extra_execution: Calling r or qokaiin returns a reference/value; IDENTIFIED_BY unifies existing terms; RECALL repeats a constraint. None allocates or performs an ENTER or a part start.
operator_application_contract.source_cases: Use every originally owned N=2,3,4 and C0,C1,C2,C3 case separately. Keep M/P1/P2 event sequences, rests and duration assumptions unchanged. No source-prescribed finite stopping time is added.
operator_application_contract.polarity_distribution: The new extended-scope construction distributes the existing unary PROHIBIT operator over the two separately stated entry-relation assertions: PROHIBIT(R10), then WHEN(g,PROHIBIT(R11)). It is explicitly NOT the formula NOT(R10 AND R11). The short-scope variant instead gives PROHIBIT(R10), then WHEN(g,REQUIRE(R11)). This grammatical distribution/inheritance is a new assumption, not an unmentioned change to the old NOT word.
